runs.name: SpectralFormer (Cross-Band ViT)
runs.description: Hyperspectral transformer utilizing Group-wise Spectral Embedding and Cross-Layer Attention.

diagnostics.title: Generalization Gap & Overfitting Detected
diagnostics.observed_evidence: Final Train OA is 99.90% vs Val OA of 92.85% (gap: +7.05%). Validation loss rose in 4 of the last 4 observed epoch transitions.
diagnostics.recommendation: Introduce stronger regularization: increase weight decay (e.g. 1e-4 -> 1e-3), increase dropout (e.g. 0.3 -> 0.5), use label smoothing, or apply spectral-spatial data augmentations (spectral jittering, random erasing).

runs.notes: Excellent spectral attention modeling. Suffers slight spatial boundary ambiguity on fine classes (e.g. Grass-pasture-mowed) due to smaller 9x9 patch window.

diagnostics.recommendation: Introduce stronger regularization: increase weight decay (e.g. 1e-4 -> 1e-3), increase dropout (e.g. 0.3 -> 0.5), use label smoothing, or apply spectral-spatial data augmentations (spectral jittering, random erasing).

reports.title: Comparative Benchmark of Spectral-Spatial Transformers vs 3D-CNNs on AVIRIS Indian Pines
reports.abstract: This report evaluates four deep learning architectures on the Indian Pines hyperspectral dataset under rigorous disjoint spatial sampling. SSFTT achieved the top Overall Accuracy (98.42%) and Kappa (0.9820) while maintaining an order of magnitude fewer parameters (0.58M) than conventional 3D-CNNs (12.40M).
findings: SSFTT (RUN-HSI-01) dominates the Pareto efficiency curve with 98.42% OA at only 0.58M parameters and 1.84 GFLOPs.
HybridSN (RUN-HSI-02) achieved competitive 97.10% OA but requires 8.8x more parameters (5.12M) and more than double the FLOPs.
Classical 3D-CNN (RUN-HSI-04) exhibits severe compute inefficiency (8.6 GFLOPs, 18.5ms latency) without accuracy benefits.
Transformer tokenization significantly improves rare-class recall on imbalanced targets such as Oats and Alfalfa.
reports.markdown_content:
# Comparative Benchmark on AVIRIS Indian Pines

## Executive Summary
Evaluation conducted across 4 runs under strictly identical experimental conditions (Seed: 42, Disjoint spatial split 10% train / 90% test, 200 calibrated AVIRIS bands).

| Model | OA (%) | AA (%) | Kappa | Params (M) | FLOPs (G) | Latency (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SSFTT** | **98.42** | **97.80** | **0.9820** | **0.58** | **1.84** | **4.2** |
| HybridSN | 97.10 | 95.84 | 0.9669 | 5.12 | 4.20 | 9.8 |
| SpectralFormer | 96.35 | 94.70 | 0.9583 | 1.95 | 2.90 | 7.1 |
| 3D-CNN | 91.50 | 88.20 | 0.9030 | 12.40 | 8.60 | 18.5 |

### Key Takeaway
SSFTT forms the single Pareto frontier point dominating all three baselines in both classification accuracy and compute budget.
recommendations: Deploy SSFTT as the default backbone for remote sensing classification pipelines.
Investigate spectral-spatial data augmentations to close the remaining 1.58% error gap.
Evaluate 8-bit post-training quantization on SSFTT to assess latency on embedded UAV hardware.
